messages:
Lina: FYI bringing up a new candidate 'zenith-emb-v2' on staging. Quick smoke plan: wiki-50k holdout + longtail queries. Need recall@1/5/10, silhouette, and UMAP stability checks. Baseline fp16 then int8 (per-channel) and int4 (per-tensor) quant configs. Any immediate objections?

Arjun: No objections. Which ANN/index config are we using for the smoke? HNSW params matter for recall comparisons.

Lina: Good call. Default smoke will use HNSW with m=16, ef_search=64 to keep runtime down. We'll also run m=32, ef=128 for the final comparison. Eval command I'm using:

```
python eval/bench_embeddings.py \
  --model zenith-v2 \
  --dataset wiki50k_holdout \
  --index hnsw \
  --m 32 \
  --ef 128 \
  --quant int8_per_channel \
  --normalization l2
```

bench-bot: automated results posted for initial sweep (fp16 / int8_pc / int4_pt):

```
# automated bench output
Model       | Quant    | Recall@1 | Recall@5 | Recall@10 | Silhouette | Notes
zenith-v2   | fp16     | 0.762    | 0.892    | 0.927     | 0.21       | baseline
zenith-v2   | int8_pc  | 0.743    | 0.879    | 0.919     | 0.17       | small drop
zenith-v2   | int4_pt  | 0.612    | 0.760    | 0.815     | 0.05       | cluster collapse on short queries
```

Tess: Ok int8 drop is modest, expected. int4 looks catastrophic — silhouette 0.05 and notes about short queries. Did we change embedding postnorm scaling for the quantized path?

Lina: No manual rescale; we used default quant pipeline with calibration on a 5k subset. I suspected int4 would need extra tricks.

Sam: Can bench-bot slice results by query length? My hunch: short queries (<=8 tokens) lose most recall.

bench-bot: slice results attached (short/medium/long):

```
Slice      | Quant    | R@1   | R@5   | R@10
short(<=8) | fp16     | 0.720 | 0.860 | 0.902
short(<=8) | int8_pc  | 0.682 | 0.832 | 0.882
short(<=8) | int4_pt  | 0.451 | 0.610 | 0.677
med(9-32)  | int4_pt  | 0.610 | 0.768 | 0.815
long(>32)  | int4_pt  | 0.693 | 0.810 | 0.855
```

Tess: That confirms it. Short queries collapse. Likely cause: quantization zeroing small components — short queries have sparser informative signals and get pushed closer to cluster centers incorrectly.

Arjun: Two quick experiments to try: (1) per-channel residual scaling (per-row) instead of per-tensor; (2) apply L2-normalization after dequant and see if that recovers recall. Also try asymmetric vs symmetric quant for int4.

Lina: Agreed. I'll queue a sweep: int4 variants = [per-channel symmetric, per-channel asymmetric, per-tensor symmetric + post-L2 clipnorm], plus fp16 baseline and int8_pc. Also will test embedding temperature/activation clamp during calibration.

Sam: Please add a run with HNSW m=32/ef=128 for the int4 best candidate — sometimes index params hide quant effects.

bench-bot: queued jobs created: 8 runs (int4 variants x 2 index configs) + fp16/int8 control. ETA ~ 45m.

Lina: Quick note — also have a small eval of cluster metrics (ARI / silhouette per cluster) from a UMAP downsample: initial fp16 ARI=0.34, int8_pc ARI=0.31, int4_pt ARI=0.08. Will post plots when job finishes.

Tess: If per-channel symmetric helps, we should include it in the quant recommendations for embed onboarding. Also add a short sanity test for embedding norm distribution (pre/post quant) and cosine shift histogram.

Arjun: One more: try quant-aware calibration with a mixture of short queries emphasized (upsample short queries in calibration set). Might reduce the short-query regressions.

Lina: Good idea. I'll run a calibration variant that weights short queries 3x. Adding it to the queue.

bench-bot: run results completed. Summary (high level):

```
best_int4_variant = per_channel_asym + post_l2clip
best_int4_R@1 (short) = 0.594 (improved from 0.451)
overall R@1 (int4 best) = 0.688 (vs fp16 0.762)
silhouette (int4 best) = 0.15
notes: per-channel asymmetric + short-weighted calibration recovered majority of short-query loss, still ~7% absolute R@1 gap vs fp16
```

Sam: That's promising. Can we also run a 1k-sample manual inspect of nearest neighbors for failure cases? I'd like to see qualitative shifts (stopwords/anchors).

Lina: Will create a small html viz of NN lists and UMAP plots. Posting link here when ready. Also will open a ticket to track: onboarding-zenith-v2 -> quant-recommendations.

Tess: TL;DR: int8 looks ok; int4 requires per-channel asymmetric + short-query-weighted calibration + post-L2 clip to be usable. Add these to the onboarding checklist if we promote zenith.

Arjun: Sounds like an action plan. I'll run one more HNSW scaling test overnight with ef=256 to ensure top-k stability.

Lina: Thanks all — will post artifacts (plots + viz + ticket) in this thread when done. @Arjun @Tess @Sam :eyes:
